title: Canary experiments observability guidelines
body:
Purpose:
This note defines a lightweight but practical observability approach for canary experiments (model rollouts, routing changes, batching policies, quantization flags) with emphasis on: measurable SLI surface, low-cost tracing, dashboarding minimalism for fast operator decisions, and instrumentation trade-offs to control query and storage budget.

Scope:
- Applies to 1) model variant canaries (new quantized model, different tokenization), 2) routing policy canaries (region fallback, cost-tier routing), 3) config canaries (batching/timeout/kv-cache tweaks).
- Not a full incident response playbook — this complements the incident/runbook docs.

Success criteria for a canary run (examples):
- Clear signal separation between control and canary cohorts in metric windows (p99 latency delta < 10ms expected for lightweight changes).
- No increase in hallucination/quality regressions above baseline evaluation sets (evaluations run via Optimize).
- Traceable error surface: >90% of errors attributable to single span or component after trace sampling.
- Cost delta measured and bounded (token-cost and telemetry-cost).

Quick definitions (keep these versioned):
- Canary cohort: fraction of traffic routed to new variant. Always tag requests with canary_id and cohort (control|canary).
- Canary window: pre-defined time window (min 30m, typical 2–6h) for initial evaluation.
- Canary metrics: core metrics used to decide pass/fail (see below).

Core metrics (SLIs) to capture for every canary:
- Latency: request_latency_p50/p90/p99 (end-to-end server-side). Tag by model, route, canary_id, cohort, tenant_type.
- Token per request: avg_tokens_requested, avg_tokens_generated (to catch prompt changes or truncation).
- Error rate: request_error_rate (5xx, model_timeouts, tokenizer_errors) with breakdown by span tag.
- Quality proxy: rerank_score_drop_percent or eval_set_pass_rate (when applicable) — keep small eval set run during canary to catch regressions early.
- Cost proxy: tokens_billed_per_minute, GPU_seconds_per_minute (for Dedicated), telemetry_ingest_mb_per_minute.
- Cache metrics: kv_cache_hit_rate, prefix_cache_evictions (for cache/tuning canaries).

Tracing guidance (low overhead):
- Minimal span set for canary observability: entry (http.request), model.infer (batched), runtime.kv_lookup, tokenizer.encode, tokenizer.decode, model.compile (if triggered), fallback.selector.
- Add a canary_id and cohort attribute to root span and propagate to child spans. This enables trace-driven comparison.
- Adaptive sampling: sample 100% of error traces for the canary cohort (we want full coverage of failures) and ~1% of success traces; for high-traffic endpoints increase to 5% success sample for canary cohort only.
- Span tagging hygiene: avoid high-cardinality free-text tags on canary traces (do not tag entire prompt). Use hash of prompt fingerprint if necessary (prompt_fp).
- Debug traces: allow temporary 100% sampling for a short debug window (must be gated, via feature flag).

Dashboard and widgets (operator-focused compact layout):
Top row: quick health snapshot
- small tile: canary pass/fail boolean (computed by evaluation pipeline)
- p99 latency delta (canary vs control) with sparkline
- error rate delta (stacked by error kind)

Middle row: detailed decomposition
- heatmap: latency slice by request size (tokens_in x tokens_out) split by cohort
- stacked bar: token consumption and GPU seconds (cost proxy) per cohort
- timeseries: kv_cache_hit_rate and prefix_cache_evictions (for cache-related canaries)

Bottom row: traces and quality
- sample trace list pinned to canary cohort (links to full trace viewer), with quick filters for error/span type
- small table: eval_set results (pass rate, top-3 failing prompts)

Design notes for dashboards:
- Single dashboard per canary run (named canary/{canary_id}) — easier to snapshot and archive.
- Widgets should default to cohort-level aggregation; drilldowns to tenant, route, or GPU pool optional.
- Keep dashboard query window small by default (last 2h) with quick presets (2h, 6h, 24h).

Sampling and cost-control rules:
- Telemetry budget check before scheduling canary: estimate ingestion increase from higher trace sampling and eval runs. Add budget to the ticket.
- Instrumentation trade-offs for low-cost canaries: prioritize error trace capture and latency histograms. Defer full request-body capture unless debugging.
- Cardinality guardrails: limit cohort-level tags; use bucketed values where possible (e.g., request_size_bucket: 0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024).

Rollout instrumentation checklist (pre/during/post):
- Pre-canary (must): create canary dashboard, register canary_id in metadata store, attach minimal eval set, set sampling policy, configure cohort tag propagation, ensure alert overrides for canary sensitivity (mute non-actionable alerts).
- During canary: monitor core SLI tiles every 15m for first hour, check traces for new error classes, check cost proxies, run quick manual prompt replay for top failing prompts.
- Post-canary: snapshot dashboard, export traces for failures, run full eval sweep if canary passes, annotate the deployment ticket with pass/fail and telemetry artifacts.

Alerting and thresholds (suggested starting points — tune per route):
- Latency: alert if p99_canary > p99_control + 25ms AND relative increase > 10% for 10m
- Error: alert if request_error_rate_canary > request_error_rate_control + 0.5 percentage points AND absolute > 1%
- Quality eval: alert if eval_pass_rate_canary < eval_pass_rate_control - 3%
- Cost: alert if tokens_billed_per_minute increases > 15% and GPU_seconds_per_minute increases > 10% (signal for inefficient model).

Investigation playbook snippets (quick wins):
- If latency regresses and p99 jump is isolated to larger prompts: check batching distribution and model.infer span durations; compare batch size histograms between cohorts.
- If error rate increases but traces show tokenizer.decode errors: compare tokenizer version tags and look for truncation changes in prompt_fp counts.
- If quality drop but latency same: run eval_set with debug sampling ON, capture top 50 failing prompts, and run deterministic reproduction on local infra.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want automatic canary score computation in Console (composite of SLI deltas + eval result)? (TODO @product)
- Where to persist canary dashboards long-term (observability archive or attach to deployment ticket)? (TODO @platform)
- Small experiment: try median-based SLOs for cache warmup detection — design metric bucket mapping. (TODO @eng-obs)

Appendix: example quick queries (pseudo-sql-like)
- p99 latency delta: SELECT quantile(0.99, latency_ms) BY cohort, model WHERE canary_id = 'C-2026-031'
- error rate: SELECT count_if(status >= 500)/count(*) BY cohort WHERE canary_id = 'C-2026-031'

Notes to self / rough log: 
- 2025-11-12: initial draft after SRE-run with Maya; focused on tracing sampling debate.
- 2026-01-08: added cost-control section after Dedicated billing spike during a QA run.
- 2026-02-20: Julian suggested cohort-level dashboards to reduce dashboard churn.

Contact: Aisha Martinez (aisha@redwood.ai) — reach out for walk-throughs or to add a canary template.
